source_review.notes: Checked current ISO 15288:2023 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 catalog metadata; NASA handbook and Stakeholder Expectations Definition guidance; and SEBoK 2.14 Identifying and Understanding Problems and Opportunities and Business or Mission Analysis pages. NASA and SEBoK links returned HTTP 200; both ISO pages returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client but current official metadata was independently retrieved. Rittel/Webber and Checkland claims are edition-bounded foundational references.

evidence: Reviewed problem-frame and frame-record tuples, stakeholder-indexed outcome gaps, intervention/counterfactual effect notation, alternative mechanism set, and solution-neutral need representation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every symbol is introduced before use; observations, desired values, causal hypotheses, counterfactual effects, constraints, and realizations remain distinct.

evidence: Executed problem-frame-record-check under Python 3.14.4 and independently recomputed three frames, one complete declared frame, missing evidence F-access, missing affected non-users F-congestion, one F-access mobile-app lexical signal, and three learning-question records.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The checker is exact for declared fields and its short phrase list only; no semantic completeness, causal validity, stakeholder legitimacy, or decision readiness is inferred.

evidence: Checked the separation of observed gap, mechanism hypothesis, and intervention hypothesis and re-derived the stakeholder outcome-gap form.
Verified that causal effect requires an unobserved counterfactual and that a solution-neutral need excludes realization except where an authorized constraint supports it.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The notation is a reasoning discipline, not a theorem that identifies causes, counterfactuals, stakeholder value, or adequate scope.

evidence: Reviewed absent data, affected non-users, power imbalance, exported harm, distribution tails, proxy gaming, multiple mechanisms, feedback, common causes, genuine versus alleged mandates, no-build alternatives, reversible versus irreversible commitments, dissent, causal confounding, lifecycle, and high-consequence cases.
Challenged all ten examples and five answers for solution bias, sponsor framing, single-root-cause claims, premature narrowing, weak counterfactuals, and unsupported external authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: A narrow next-action boundary is allowed only while the wider problem situation and exported effects remain explicit and governed.

evidence: Traced separation, plurality, boundary, neutrality, and learning invariants through exposition, ten worked examples, and five complete answers.
Verified distinct problem, effectiveness, performance, leading, distributional, and guardrail measurement roles.
invariant_checking.notes: Every frame preserves observation, interpretation, value, alternatives, uncertainty, evidence limits, decision authority, and reframing triggers.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states conditional framing relations and causal requirements but presents no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed uses of fact, evidence, cause, root cause, effect, prove, validate, legitimate, equitable, safe, mandated, complete, and neutral.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-010/report.json records exact local execution evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes declared-record and lexical observations only. It cannot establish causal mechanisms, intervention effects, stakeholder value, legal authority, safety, equity, clinical benefit, or external review.

conceptual_review.notes: Professor-style review checked problem/opportunity, situation, symptom, mechanism, need, objective, constraint, counterfactual, boundary, power, measures, solution neutrality, intervention classes, frame adequacy, learning, and reframing for conceptual consistency.

practitioner_review.notes: Practitioner-style review checked water outages, congestion, incident response, hospital flow, mandated interfaces, operator-error investigations, energy flexibility, AI triage, contested river control, medication safety, freight, deployment failure, public access, and clinical scheduling. Each example exposes assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Pedagogical review confirmed progression from situation evidence through mechanisms, values/power, boundary/counterfactuals, measurement, frame records, solution-neutral needs, option classes, executable checks, learning, and versioned reframing. Ten examples and five complete answers require reframing, diagnosis, causal modeling, measurement design, and high-consequence review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
